For the Petitioner : Mr. Binod Kumar Dubey, Advocate For the Opp. Parties : Mr. Mithilesh Singh,
G.A-IV -----------
th 08/Dated: 17 February, 2023 It is a case where the proceeding to initiate contempt has been filed for alleged willful and deliberate non-compliance of the order dated 09.07.2019 passed by the writ Court in W.P.(C) No.5859 of 2018.

The issue basis upon which the writ Court has passed an order is based upon the claim of the petitioner that the land in question in which the petitioner is in possession for last 30 years and his name has also been entered in the Register-II but even then while making acquisition of land in order to hand over to the Indian Railway, the State Government has not paid a single penny against the compensation in lieu of the aforesaid acquisition.
The writ Court has passed an order directing the State authority to take decision regarding the claim of the petitioner.

The matter was heard on several dates and finally a show cause has been filed wherein reference of a decision taken by the committee on 02.01.2023 by which the claim of compensation to be made in favour of the petitioner has been rejected on the ground that the case of the petitioner is not falling for its consideration under the circular dated 14.05.2009 as appended under Annexure-B series to the supplementary show cause filed on 10.01.2023.

It appears from the order passed by the committee dated 02.01.2023 that although the case of the petitioner has been examined in the light of the Government notification dated 16.08.2013 issued by the Revenue and Land Reforms Department wherein it has been found that the Jamabandi said to Mangar Mian vs The State Of Jharkhand & Ors. ...... Opp. ... on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71899606/
1 have been not found in the name of the petitioner for last 30 years as recorded in the Register-II rather it is running from last 28 to 29 years.
This Court, on perusal of the order passed by the committee dated 02.01.2023, has failed to understand that if the land of the petitioner has been shown to have entered in the Register-II then where is the question to deny the compensation to the petitioner on the ground that Jamabandi so created in favour of the petitioner in the Register-II is running only for 28-29 years and not completed the period of 30 years.
This Court has posed a question that why there is reference of decision of Jamabandi less than 30 years referred in Register-II has posed a question that if the Jamabandi has been created in favour of the petitioner irrespective of the period then where is the question of applicability of the notification dated 16.08.2013.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the State, as would appear from the order dated 02.01.2023, that the Jamabandi has been created in favour of the petitioner as referred in Register-II then the proper course for acquisition would have been to issue notice under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.
Considering the same, the decision so taken cannot be said to be compliance in the eye of law.

Since,
compliance of the order will only be said to be compliance if the same is in accordance with law.

This Court, has also posed a question that at the time of making requisition for acquisition of land to be transferred in favour of the Indian Railway, is desirous to know as to whether the Indian Railway while furnishing the amount for acquisition of land also includes the area of the land, which is the subject matter of this litigation having been acquired which was in possession of the petitioner.
Let the Opposite Party No.2 file further show cause affidavit explaining the aforesaid fact/legal issues on or before the next date of hearing.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) Saket/-
